heading: Flood Fill = DFS Recoloring
body:
**Flood fill** spreads from a starting pixel to all 4-connected neighbors with the **same original color**. Use **DFS** to recursively visit each matching pixel, recolor it, and explore up/down/left/right.

**Critical guard:** if `originalColor == newColor`, return immediately—otherwise infinite recursion!

heading: Recognize 4-Connected Spread Problems
body:
Classic signal: **"change all connected cells"** in a grid. Paint bucket tools, island expansion, spreading infection/fire.

Key: track the **original value** before you mutate it, then DFS in 4 directions checking bounds and matching color.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why must we check if the original color equals the new color before starting the DFS?
options: To avoid infinite recursion since pixels would never change color
To optimize the algorithm's time complexity
To ensure the starting pixel is within bounds
To prevent stack overflow from visiting too many pixels
explain: If the original color equals the new color, pixels will never change color—DFS would revisit the same pixels repeatedly, causing infinite recursion.
